pr.body:
## What does this PR do?

- generate and display backup codes during 2fa setup
- enable their use during 2fa login flow
- fix 2fa setup test to include new backup code screen

[backup-codes-setup.webm](https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/assets/55853254/3bebfb21-f7ef-4717-9135-ac30387cfb18)

[backup-codes-login.webm](https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/assets/55853254/71ef61b1-af6f-4e32-bf1e-455e52560535)

Fixes #9910
/claim #9910

## Type of change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

## How should this be tested?

1. Setup 2fa to see the generated backup codes
2. Try to login with them by clicking on "Lost access"

## Mandatory Tasks

- [x] Make sure you have self-reviewed the code. A decent size PR without self-review might be rejected.

## Checklist

- I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
pr.title: feat: 2fa backup codes

raw_findings.body: A single leaked static backup code grants full account login without ever verifying the account password, weakening 2FA into a one-static-secret bypass.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Authentication succeeds with only a long-lived static backup code, bypassing the password factor entirely.
raw_findings.impact: A single leaked static backup code grants full account login without ever verifying the account password, weakening 2FA into a one-static-secret bypass.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new backup-code branch is evaluated whenever credentials.backupCode is truthy and ignores totpCode, while password verification is skipped whenever totpCode is present, so no first factor is ever checked on this path.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: In the backup-code branch, require and verify the account password (or restrict the password-skip path to the verified totpEmail flow), e.g. verify credentials.password against user.password before accepting a backup code.
raw_findings.title: Backup-code login skips password verification when a dummy totpCode is also supplied
raw_findings.trigger: An attacker who obtained a victim's downloaded backup-codes file POSTs credentials with email, any non-empty totpCode (e.g. "1"), and a valid backupCode. The pre-existing guard `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)` skips password verification because totpCode is truthy, and the new backup-code branch takes precedence over the TOTP branch, never validating totpCode.

raw_findings.body: A genuinely valid backup code is rejected with IncorrectBackupCode, locking a user who lost their authenticator out of their account.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Legitimate recovery login fails for case-variant input, defeating the purpose of backup codes.
raw_findings.impact: A genuinely valid backup code is rejected with IncorrectBackupCode, locking a user who lost their authenticator out of their account.
raw_findings.root_cause: String comparison of user-typed input against lowercase hex codes without case normalization.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Normalize with `.toLowerCase()` (in addition to stripping dashes) before the indexOf comparison.
raw_findings.title: Backup code comparison is case-sensitive during login, rejecting hand-typed uppercase codes
raw_findings.trigger: Codes are generated as lowercase hex (crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")), but the login input placeholder is "XXXXX-XXXXX"; a user who retypes a printed/stored code in uppercase (e.g. "AB12C-D34EF") submits it during backup-code login.

raw_findings.body: The disable request fails with IncorrectBackupCode even though the code is valid, preventing the user from disabling 2FA after losing their authenticator.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Valid recovery codes are rejected in the disable-2FA flow.
raw_findings.impact: The disable request fails with IncorrectBackupCode even though the code is valid, preventing the user from disabling 2FA after losing their authenticator.
raw_findings.root_cause: Case-sensitive comparison of user-typed input against lowercase-hex stored codes, duplicated from the login path.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Lowercase req.body.backupCode before stripping dashes and comparing against the stored codes.
raw_findings.title: Backup code comparison is case-sensitive in the 2FA disable endpoint
raw_findings.trigger: A user disabling 2FA via the "Lost access" flow types a stored backup code in uppercase (input placeholder shows "XXXXX-XXXXX") while stored codes are lowercase hex.

raw_findings.body: The handler throws an unhandled TypeError and the API responds with a 500 instead of a 400 validation error.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Malformed request bodies crash the request with an internal server error.
raw_findings.impact: The handler throws an unhandled TypeError and the API responds with a 500 instead of a 400 validation error.
raw_findings.root_cause: New code calls a string method on unvalidated JSON body input.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Validate req.body.backupCode is a string (e.g. via a zod schema or `typeof req.body.backupCode === "string"`) before calling replaceAll.
raw_findings.title: Non-string backupCode in request body causes unhandled TypeError (500) in disable endpoint
raw_findings.trigger: A POST to /api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable with a truthy non-string backupCode (e.g. `{"backupCode": 123}` or an array) passes the `req.body.backupCode` truthiness gate, then `.replaceAll` is not a function on that value.

raw_findings.body: The documented "each backup code can be used exactly once" guarantee is violated: a code can be replayed within the race window, and concurrent use of two different codes can lose one consumption (last write wins).
raw_findings.failure_mode: Single-use invariant of backup codes is not enforced under concurrent logins.
raw_findings.impact: The documented "each backup code can be used exactly once" guarantee is violated: a code can be replayed within the race window, and concurrent use of two different codes can lose one consumption (last write wins).
raw_findings.root_cause: Decrypt-check-null-reencrypt sequence performed without any locking, transaction, or optimistic-concurrency guard.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Consume the code atomically, e.g. use a transaction with a conditional update (updateMany matching the old encrypted value / a version field) and fail the login if no row was updated.
raw_findings.title: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write, allowing concurrent reuse of a single-use code
raw_findings.trigger: Two login requests presenting the same backup code arrive concurrently; both decrypt the same stored list, both find the code via indexOf before either update commits, and both authorize.

raw_findings.body: The two-factor switch still shows unchecked because viewer.me is never invalidated even though 2FA is enabled, and reopening the modal jumps straight to the stale DisplayBackupCodes step (with no Cancel button) instead of ConfirmPassword.
raw_findings.failure_mode: UI state (switch, modal step) diverges from actual server-side 2FA state after a common dismissal gesture.
raw_findings.impact: The two-factor switch still shows unchecked because viewer.me is never invalidated even though 2FA is enabled, and reopening the modal jumps straight to the stale DisplayBackupCodes step (with no Cancel button) instead of ConfirmPassword.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch replaced the immediate onEnable() on success with a new intermediate step whose completion is only wired to the explicit Close button, not to dialog dismissal.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Handle dialog dismissal on the DisplayBackupCodes step (e.g. in onOpenChange) by calling resetState() and onEnable(), or prevent dismissal until the user clicks Close.
raw_findings.title: Dismissing the enable-2FA dialog on the backup-codes step skips onEnable, leaving stale UI state
raw_findings.trigger: After entering a valid TOTP code, 2FA is already enabled server-side and the modal moves to DisplayBackupCodes; the user then closes the dialog via Escape or the overlay (Dialog onOpenChange) instead of the "Close" button, so neither resetState() nor onEnable() runs.

validated_findings.body: The documented "each backup code can be used exactly once" guarantee is violated: a code can be replayed within the race window, and concurrent use of two different codes can lose one consumption (last write wins).
validated_findings.failure_mode: Single-use invariant of backup codes is not enforced under concurrent logins.
validated_findings.impact: The documented "each backup code can be used exactly once" guarantee is violated: a code can be replayed within the race window, and concurrent use of two different codes can lose one consumption (last write wins).
validated_findings.root_cause: Decrypt-check-null-reencrypt sequence performed without any locking, transaction, or optimistic-concurrency guard.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Consume the code atomically, e.g. use a transaction with a conditional update (updateMany matching the old encrypted value / a version field) and fail the login if no row was updated.
validated_findings.title: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write, allowing concurrent reuse of a single-use code
validated_findings.trigger: Two login requests presenting the same backup code arrive concurrently; both decrypt the same stored list, both find the code via indexOf before either update commits, and both authorize.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 144-156 show a read-modify-write pattern: indexOf check, then null assignment, then prisma.user.update. No transaction or optimistic locking is used. Two concurrent requests with the same backup code could both pass the indexOf check before either update commits, allowing code reuse. This is a valid race condition in the new code.

validated_findings.body: The two-factor switch still shows unchecked because viewer.me is never invalidated even though 2FA is enabled, and reopening the modal jumps straight to the stale DisplayBackupCodes step (with no Cancel button) instead of ConfirmPassword.
validated_findings.failure_mode: UI state (switch, modal step) diverges from actual server-side 2FA state after a common dismissal gesture.
validated_findings.impact: The two-factor switch still shows unchecked because viewer.me is never invalidated even though 2FA is enabled, and reopening the modal jumps straight to the stale DisplayBackupCodes step (with no Cancel button) instead of ConfirmPassword.
validated_findings.root_cause: The patch replaced the immediate onEnable() on success with a new intermediate step whose completion is only wired to the explicit Close button, not to dialog dismissal.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Handle dialog dismissal on the DisplayBackupCodes step (e.g. in onOpenChange) by calling resetState() and onEnable(), or prevent dismissal until the user clicks Close.
validated_findings.title: Dismissing the enable-2FA dialog on the backup-codes step skips onEnable, leaving stale UI state
validated_findings.trigger: After entering a valid TOTP code, 2FA is already enabled server-side and the modal moves to DisplayBackupCodes; the user then closes the dialog via Escape or the overlay (Dialog onOpenChange) instead of the "Close" button, so neither resetState() nor onEnable() runs.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 135 shows `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)` replacing the previous `onEnable()` call. The onEnable callback (which invalidates viewer.me per line 67 in two-factor-auth.tsx) is now only called in the Close button handler. If user dismisses via Escape/overlay, onEnable never runs and the switch state won't update. The patch introduces this by changing the flow.

validated_findings.title: New backup-code login and disable paths ship without any automated test coverage

validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a test coverage gap finding. The TODO comment at line 12 acknowledges missing tests, but absence of tests is not a defect in the code itself. The finding describes potential future regressions rather than a concrete bug introduced by the patch. Test gap findings are typically considered stylistic/process issues rather than code defects.
